newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks steady in morning, await HSBC results.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks steady in morning, await HSBC results.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were steady in Monday morning trade, with the market awaiting HSBC Holdings results due later and some investors sidelined ahead of a busy schedule of U.S. data due this week.
The Hang Seng Index was up 18.27 points, or 0.14 percent, at 13,416.99 after dipping to an early low of 13,354.55.
Turnover was HK$2.22 billion after the first 50 minutes of trade.
"The market is going to be a bit wishy-washy. People are wondering about HSBC results. Once we get that out of the way we will probably see a rally," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
HSBC Holdings Plc is expected to announce a rise of more than 20 percent in 1996 net profit from the HK$30.04 billion reported for 1995, analysts said.
"If the result goes beyond that, we may see some strong buying taking the stock to the HK$200 level," said one analyst.
HSBC shares rose HK$0.50 to HK$189.50 in early trade.
Hang Seng Bank is also due to announce its 1996 results later. Analysts expect net profit of about HK$9.3 billion, up 16 percent compared with 1995's HK$7.98 billion.
The stock was down HK$0.75 at HK$88.75 in morning trade.
Ricky Tam, research manger at Delta Asia Securities, said the futures market was trading at a discount to cash, limiting the market's upside.
March Hang Seng Index futures were up 78 points at 13,348.
"There is a lot of uncertainty," he said, pointing to a slew of U.S. economic data due this week, including February employment data on Friday.
"This week a lot of investors will stay on the sidelines," said Tam. "I think the market might hold 13,300 for a few days but at the end of the week the market will maybe test 13,000," he added.
Shares in Great Eagle Holdings rose HK$0.90 to HK$29.95. The company said it had decided not to go ahead with the proposed spin off of its Tai Shan Properties unit.
"What would have been left after the Tai Shan Properties spin off? Not a lot," said Osborn.
"And as a result there is a feeling that actually in many ways, although they were going to raise a lot of money, in the short term there is probably a bit of upside potential."
First Pacific is due to release final results on Monday. The stock was steady at HK$10.85.
